fieldValues.title: Successor 'example' leaves from the section/subsection split can be left parented only under the record being retired, with no derived-from edge at all
fieldValues.summary: Across all 18 subsections whose prose was already relocated to mechanism successors (batches #561-564/#687/#686), the fenced-code-block 'example' leaves extracted from that prose were attached via `contains` directly to the subsection being retired and never reparented to the subsection's replacement concept, and carry no `derived-from` relation to the subsection at all (unlike sibling mechanism leaves, which do). Deleting the subsection via `record delete --cascade` without first reparenting these leaves would silently orphan them.
evidence: Scanned all 61 subsection records still typed `com.semanticops.spec/subsection` on origin/master (c3c5b02): 18 have fieldValues.content replaced with a 'Content relocated to... See derived-from' stub.

Across those 18, found 61 total inbound `contains` relations sourced from the subsection itself, targeting 61 distinct records -- zero of which also carry a second, non-subsection `contains` parent (checked every one's full inbound relation list).

Cross-referenced against the 121 records that DO carry a `derived-from` edge to one of these 18 subsections: zero overlap with the 61 orphaned children -- confirming the orphans are a structurally distinct, unrelated-by-provenance set of leaves, not double-counted successors.

Example: subsection 136187cc (ext:slices) has 6 mechanism successors (each derived-from + properly contains-parented under concept 23f7a465 'Travelling form') plus 1 example leaf (3d8bd905, 'The `slice` manifest property') that had only the subsection's own `contains` edge and no derived-from edge at all -- confirmed by content match that it belongs under the same concept.

This PR (the-greenman/srs#745) fixed 8 of the 61 (across 6 subsections); 53 remain across the other 12 already-migrated subsections, plus an unknown number likely to appear in the 43 not-yet-migrated subsections once they are split.
fieldValues.body:
The pattern: when a subsection's prose was split (batches #561-564), any fenced code block became its own `example` record via `contains` from the SUBSECTION being retired, while the surrounding prose became `mechanism` records with a proper `derived-from` edge to the subsection AND a proper `contains` edge to the subsection's replacement concept. The example leaves got only the first half of that treatment.

Why this matters for the remaining `srs#710` work: `record delete --cascade` will happily delete the subsection and silently remove that `contains` edge along with everything else in `cascadedRelations` -- there is no error, no warning, nothing that would catch an unreparented leaf being orphaned. The only way to catch it is to check BEFORE deleting: for every successor (found either via `derived-from` OR via the subsection's own outbound `contains`), confirm it has a second, non-subsection `contains` parent.

Recommendation for the next unit continuing srs#710: before choosing which subsections to finalize, run the same check this unit ran (scan every remaining subsection's outbound `contains` edges, not just its inbound `derived-from` edges) and budget time to reparent any orphaned leaves found, using the target concept indicated by content/title match against already-properly-parented siblings.
